title: RAW UNREVIEWED: keep botanical comparison distinct from the plant part used in an operation
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In the retained complete critical-edition text of Dioscorides II.162 (Ptarmike), a single plant-description block first compares branches to abrotonon, leaves to olive, and the terminal head to anthemis; it then assigns a poultice made with leaves plus flowers to removing under-eye bruising, assigns flowers alone to provoking sneezing, and closes with habitat. The proposal is an entity-centered multi-step route: description/comparison groups identify the plant and its organs, while later whole-form groups encode actual material/operation/effect relations. A comparator is not automatically an ingredient or a second plant. Morgan M.652 f138r locally verifies these clauses as a whole block, but the retained source dossier does not claim a complete diplomatic transcript. No Voynich target span was accessed or mapped; exact target owners, word meanings, event grouping and construction-to-role mapping remain unknown. Rival: comparison strings may function as copied names/ingredients, or the action clauses may belong to separate entries. Smallest reading consequence, if a future already-admitted whole account supports it: change one comparison-bearing candidate whole form from an ingredient to a descriptive comparator, and preserve the independently stated leaf+flower and flower-only operation groups. This is not a word gloss or confirmed binding.

design.mechanism: A persistent plant referent spans a comparison-rich identification stage and later typed operations. Directed component composition may constrain ordering; the exact whole-form residual and entry context must distinguish comparison/attribute material from ingredient, operation, and outcome. No EVA element is assigned a semantic value.
design.unit: Whole Ptarmike entry II.162 in H_COMPLETE_ENTRIES.md, from opening description through the two organ-specific efficacy statements and habitat clause. Source layer is Wellmann 1907–1914 critical-edition XML cache, not a fresh diplomatic transcription of Morgan M.652. The retained dossier states that comparator, two efficacy clauses, and habitat were checked in the complete local Morgan M.652 f138r block; minor wording differences are not normalized as manuscript quotations.
design.contrast: A comparison such as “leaves like olive” is a descriptive property of the plant versus a medicinal ingredient binding such as leaves plus flowers applied to a named site, or flowers alone provoking an effect. Rival constructions collapse the comparator into material identity/recipe input or split the clauses across unrelated referents.
design.prediction: On a future whole-unit reading with no new target access, a coherent candidate must keep one plant owner through description and use; attach comparison clauses to morphology; preserve the leaf+flower poultice and flower-only sneezing operations as separate role sets; and leave the habitat clause as location rather than an application. If it cannot preserve all groups without relabeling the comparator as an ingredient or inventing a second plant referent, the route fails. GDT608 justifies testing directed structure plus whole-form residuals; it supplies no meanings.
design.scope: Exploratory raw source-model only. No target folio, exact Voynich form, or semantic value is selected. Unknown: what admitted Voynich whole unit (if any) has compatible group structure; whether any repeated whole-form differences separate comparison from operation; binding of plant, organ, comparator, recipient, effect, and habitat; whether the critical edition wording matches the manuscript exactly. This differs from AL glossary continuation and from IDEA427/429 abstract phase/family slots; it does not claim novelty merely from search rank.

source_evidence.quote:
162 πταρμικὴ θαμνίον ἐστί ... ὅθεν καὶ ὠνόμασται.
δύναμιν δὲ ἔχει καταπλασσόμενα τὰ φύλλα μετὰ τῶν ἀνθῶν ὑπώπια αἴρειν. τὰ δὲ ἄνθη πταρμοὺς ἐνεργέστατα κινεῖ, φύεται δὲ ἐν ὀρεινοῖς καὶ πετρώδεσι τόποις.
